node-1.label: A man in his 50s presented with a 5-week history of right facial paresis, facial numbness, and severe ipsilateral headaches

node-2.label: He presented to an outside ED shortly after onset and was treated with an unknown antibiotic without steroids; medical history included poorly controlled diabetes mellitus and hypothyroidism

node-3.label: Physical exam showed right-sided chemosis and exophthalmos, purulent nasal secretions, maxillary nerve hypoesthesia, complete eye closure with effort, moderate brow weakness, lip droop with effort (House-Brackmann III right facial paresis), and intact left facial nerve

node-4.label: Nasal endoscopy revealed polypoid changes of the right middle turbinate and purulence within the nasal cavity, with no necrotic debris observed

why.why: Negative fungal cultures, in addition to the absence of fungus on biopsy and growth of coagulase-negative Staphylococcus and Enterococcus faecalis, effectively exclude rhinocerebral fungal infection. All expert analyses uniformly conclude that fungal infection is excluded, so confidence is reduced from 0.02 to 0.01.

Radiologist, Pathologist, and Laboratory Physician analyses uniformly confirm that CT evidence of an orbital abscess with bony erosion, biopsy showing fibropurulent inflammation without fungus, and cultures growing coagulase-negative Staphylococcus and Enterococcus faecalis strongly support complicated bacterial sinusitis. The additional negative fungal cultures further exclude fungal infection, and WBC at high-normal supports a bacterial etiology, increasing confidence from 0.88 to 0.90.

Biopsy shows chronic inflammation without tumor, and the imaging and pathological findings are explained by bacterial abscess formation. Expert analyses consider malignancy less likely given the inflammatory pathology, so confidence is reduced from 0.15 to 0.05.

Although biopsy shows chronic inflammation, the presence of an orbital abscess, fibropurulent exudate, and positive bacterial cultures indicates an infectious rather than a primary non-infectious orbital inflammatory process. Expert analyses favor bacterial sinusitis, so confidence is reduced from 0.15 to 0.08.

node-9.label: CT shows right orbital abscess arising from rhinosinusitis with bony erosion but intact lamina papyracea

node-10.label: Biopsy shows chronic inflammation and fibropurulent exudate without fungus

node-11.label: Cultures grow coagulase-negative Staphylococcus and Enterococcus faecalis

node-12.label: Orbital abscess secondary to bacterial rhinosinusitis

why.why: The specific diagnosis of orbital abscess secondary to bacterial rhinosinusitis is confirmed by CT showing a right orbital abscess arising from rhinosinusitis, biopsy showing fibropurulent inflammation without fungus, and cultures growing coagulase-negative Staphylococcus and Enterococcus faecalis. Expert analyses explicitly conclude bacterial orbital abscess, and negative fungal cultures plus high-normal WBC add supporting evidence, increasing confidence from 0.85 to 0.88.
